page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5ge.12xlarge is a dedicated compute and storage instance built on the KVM hypervisor. Its compute subsystem utilizes the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs and 288.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a memory-to-core ratio of 6.0 GB per vCPU. This dedicated compute allocation delivers sustained processing performance without shared CPU overhead.

A central feature of the ecs.i5ge.12xlarge is its bundled local storage and networking capabilities. The instance includes 7679 GB of local SSD capacity directly attached to the host, bypassing network-attached storage latency for intensive disk operations. Network communication is backed by an 84 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation. The instance features no discrete GPU hardware and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high co-location of 7679 GB of local solid-state storage with balanced memory and dedicated compute minimizes the need to configure complex external storage volumes for high-throughput applications. Tradeoffs include the non-persistent nature typical of ephemeral local storage environments and the lack of hardware accelerators. This configuration is aligned with high-performance transactional databases, distributed data stores, real-time log analytics, search indexing, and large-scale ETL pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i5ge.12xlarge is a storage-focused instance type within the local SSD family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs from an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, accompanied by 288.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 6.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware provisioning includes 7679 GB of integrated local SSD storage alongside an 84 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, with no integrated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. By bundling high-capacity local solid-state storage with dedicated enterprise compute and substantial memory density, this configuration avoids off-host network storage latency bottlenecks. Consequently, the instance is well suited for demanding data-intensive applications, including distributed NoSQL databases, transactional processing engines, high-speed caching clusters, log search systems, and large-scale extract, transform, and load pipelines requiring high local disk input and output throughput.
